text:
A rate rise changes the price of every house without touching a single brick.

The Federal Reserve raised its policy rate from near zero to 5.25–5.5% between March 2022 and July 2023. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate follows ten-year Treasury yields more closely than it follows Fed announcements. It climbed from roughly 3% to above 7%.

On a $400,000 loan, that moved the monthly payment from about $1,686 to $2,661. Buyers found that their borrowing power had shrunk by more than a third. Affordability calculations no longer supported the old prices.

Owners with loans below 4% stayed where they were. This "golden handcuffs" lock-in kept the number of homes for sale low.

Sales stopped before prices fell. US existing-home sales dropped to 4.09 million in 2023, the lowest since 1995.

Credit is the market's oxygen. Higher rates ration it, and demand struggles to breathe.
